rows.note: Use this for a country forcibly absorbing another country's territory; it does not mean a book appendix or a building extension.

example.english: They used military force to annex a neighboring country.
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 jung6 mou5 lik6 tan1 bing3 leon4 gwok3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice when something is added to and incorporated into a larger territory or organization.

example.english: The city government plans to annex this plot of land to the urban area.
example.traditional: 市政府計劃將呢幅地併入市區範圍。
example.jyutping: si5 zing3 fu2 gai3 waak6 zoeng1 ne1 fuk1 dei6 bing3 jap6 si5 keoi1 faan6 wai4

rows.note: Use this when the annexation suggests taking over or absorbing another territory, especially by force.

example.english: The powerful country sent troops to annex its neighbouring country.
example.jyutping: koeng4 gwok3 ceot1 bing1 tan1 bing3 zo2 leon4 gwok3

rows.note: Use this formal term for the political or military annexation of one territory by another.

example.english: After the war, the victor formally moved to annex the region.
example.traditional: 戰後，勝方正式兼併該地區。
example.jyutping: zin3 hau6 sing3 fong1 zing3 sik1 gim1 bing3 goi1 dei6 keoi1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose term for an appendix attached to a book or document.

example.english: Please see the annex at the end of the report.
example.traditional: 請參閱報告最後嘅附錄。
example.jyutping: cing2 caam1 jyut6 bou3 gou3 zeoi3 hau6 ge3 fu6 luk6

rows.note: Use this for the added part of a building, rather than for a document appendix or territorial takeover.

example.english: The annex behind the new school building can be used next month.
example.traditional: 新校舍後面嗰幢擴建部分，下個月就可以用喇。
example.jyutping: san1 haau6 se3 hau6 min6 go2 tong4 kwong3 gin3 bou6 fan6 haa6 go3 jyut6 zau6 ho2 ji5 jung6 laa3
